subject: Possible to arrange plots in a grid using facet_grid... but facet in x and y with one variable?

messages.author: 39eada9575564b5b
messages.subject: Possible to arrange plots in a grid using facet_grid... but facet in x and y with one variable?
parts:
library(ggplot2)



## This makes a data frame that has groups "a" to "p"
## In this example the groups are different, but
## there are only two "classes":
##       1) random normal mu=30 and sigma = 10
##       2) random normal mu=0  and sigma =  1
## In real life each group could be unique, i.e. 
## there is no systematic pattern in the real data..

df = data.frame(
loc=as.factor(rep(sample(letters[1:16]),each=10)),
a = c(rnorm(80, 30, 10), rnorm(80)),
b = runif(160,4,10))
df = df[order(df$loc),]

## Plot the data with each group in facet:
ggplot(df, aes(x=a,y=b,colour=a)) + geom_point() + 
facet_grid(loc~.)


## Now I was hoping to arrange them in a grid
## I make a "group" factor so that I could make facets 4 x 4
df$locGroup = as.factor(rep(1:4, each=40))
ggplot(df, aes(x=a,y=b,colour=a)) + geom_point() + 
facet_grid(loc~locGroup)

## Can I collapse the blank parts of the graph and make a 4 x 4 plot?

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Possible to arrange plots in a grid using facet_grid... but facet in x and y with one variable?
parts:
Gene, 

I don't think this is possible. You have unique data for each "loc". There is no way for ggplot2 to know how to put "a" next to "e", "i" and "m". The only way I can think of is to subset your data logically (a-d, e-h, i-l, m-p), plot each graph independently and use grid.arrange() to put them next to each other. You would need to tweak these plots a lot:
  • remove the legends from each plot
  • give the legend it's own space (otherwise the final graph will have a different width)
  • remove ticks and extra space between plots to make it look like a facet
  • get rid of y-axis text on most plots
All possible, just depends how much you want your graph to look like what you want. 

B

> b = runif(160,4,10))
> df = df[order(df$loc),]

> ggplot(df, aes(x=a,y=b,colour=a)) + geom_point() +
> facet_grid(loc~.)

>
> ## Now I was hoping to arrange them in a grid

> df$locGroup = as.factor(rep(1:4, each=40))
> ggplot(df, aes(x=a,y=b,colour=a)) + geom_point() +
> facet_grid(loc~locGroup)
>
> ## Can I collapse the blank parts of the graph and make a 4 x 4 plot?
>

facet_wrap(~loc, nrow=4, ncol=4)

Or if you want them columnwise, you can change the order of levels on
the faceting variable

df$loc2 <- factor(df$loc)
levels(df$loc2) <- as.vector(matrix(levels(df$loc2), 4, 4, byrow=TRUE))

facet_wrap(~loc2, nrow=4, ncol=4)

Or if the locGroup structure isn't that simple, you could create a new
variable which is the place-in-column for each locGroup

library("plyr")
df <- ddply(df, .(locGroup), mutate,
col = as.numeric(factor(loc)))

facet_grid(locGroup~col)
